title: What draws a feature (water) population entry when nothing is fishing it? E26 left this loose end: the mussel entry fell 5005 to 4701 across a year on a fort with no fishing labour at load, and nothing in the tool touched it. This watches every stocked feature entry on LAKE for a full year with the tool COMPLETELY disabled — no roster, no water job — sampling the pool every 3,000 ticks. A steady drain says something consumes the pool continuously; steps say discrete events; no movement says E26's reading needs re-examining. Two replicates.
fork: Does a feature pool drain on its own, and in what shape — which decides whether the water job must budget for it.

predictions.expects: the feature pool total falls steadily across the year, roughly linearly, with no obvious events
the total holds flat then steps down, so something specific consumes it and the step size names the consumer
the pool is flat and E26's fall came from something the tool itself did

kill_criterion: a measured drain shape on a fort with nothing fishing tells the water job what it must budget for
culling: drop a replicate on any changed save

arms.name: untouched_year
pre: local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local cfg=sw.loadConfig(); if not cfg.initialized then sw.captureDefault(cfg) end; cfg.enabled=false; cfg.groups.enabled=false; cfg.ecology.enabled=false; cfg.water.enabled=false; sw.saveConfig(cfg); sw.disableSched(); print('e31: tool fully disabled — this watches DF draw a feature pool on its own')

local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local rs=sw.getEmbarkRegions(); local parts,tot={},0; for i,pop in ipairs(df.global.world.populations.all) do if pop.population.feature_idx>=0 and sw.managedPop(pop, rs, {water=true}) and pop.quantity>0 and pop.quantity<10000001 then local c=df.creature_raw.find(pop.race); local ty=df.world_population_type[pop.type]; tot=tot+pop.quantity; if #parts<10 then parts[#parts+1]=('%s[%s]=%d'):format(c and c.creature_id or '?',ty,pop.quantity) end end end; local fish=0; for _,u in ipairs(df.global.world.units.active) do if dfhack.units.isCitizen(u) and not dfhack.units.isDead(u) then fish=fish+1 end end; print(('e31: feature_pool_total=%d citizens=%d day=%d | %s'):format(tot,fish,math.floor(df.global.cur_year_tick/1200),table.concat(parts,' ')))
